calls.head: Who drives the play: the Canadiens
calls.body: The Canadiens have been around the middle of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Maple Leafs one of the worst. Expect the Canadiens to spend more of the night in the Maple Leafs’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Newhook has two goals as the Canadiens take down the Maple Leafs
paras: Alex Newhook opened the scoring for the Canadiens early in the first, and he struck again midway through the period to make it 2-0. The Maple Leafs’ Morgan Rielly left early in the second period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was listed as day to day with a lower-body injury. Chris Kreider made it 3-0 for the Habs midway through the period, and that one stood up as the winner. William Nylander and Gavin McKenna scored 55 seconds apart early in the third to cut Montréal’s lead to 3-2, but they got no closer. Zachary Bolduc stretched the lead to 4-2 on the power play with less than eight minutes left.

The Maple Leafs had a little more of the play, but the Canadiens made their chances count. Jacob Fowler made 26 saves for the Canadiens, and Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 24 of 28 at the other end. Fowler has earned a point in nine straight starts (8-0-1). The Canadiens improved to 11-3-3, second in the Atlantic, while the Maple Leafs fell to 8-8-2, seventh in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Canadiens have points in ten straight games (8-0-2), the longest run in the league right now.
The Maple Leafs’ John Tavares was back in the lineup after missing nine games.
Auston Matthews has a point in six straight games.
The Canadiens have beaten the Maple Leafs five straight times, going back to last season.
